message.content: Webhook deliveries are retrying forever in prod instead of capping at the 30s max delay, and the on-call graph shows attempt counts climbing past 6. Find out why the backoff cap isn't holding, fix it, and make sure the test suite actually covers the cap. Take your time and check the CI history too.

content.text: Nightly history has nothing on the cap either. Wrapping up.

Done. Three things were wrong, not one:

1. **The cap was never implemented.** `retry.go:88` was still a `TODO: clamp to maxRetryDelay` — `backoffFor` doubled without bound, which is why attempt 6 produced 960s instead of 30s. Clamped inside `backoffFor` so every caller inherits it.

2. **Nothing enforced `retryAttemptCap`.** The dispatcher looped past 6 attempts entirely. It now returns `ErrRetriesExhausted` at the cap.

3. **The dead-letter path was unreachable.** `queue/consumer.go` switches on an exported `webhook.ErrRetriesExhausted`, but the dispatcher declared it unexported — so `drainOnce` could never route an exhausted delivery. Exported it.

`TestWebhookRetry_BackoffCapsAtMaxDelay` now asserts the cap at attempts 6, 9 and 14 instead of the old hardcoded 960s expectation. `backoffFor` is at 100% coverage; `webhook`, `queue` and `billing` all pass.

The CI history you asked about was a dead end — every run is green because no assertion ever covered the cap, so there was no regression point to find.
